messages.privacy.title: Privacy Policy
messages.privacy.meta-description: How MicCamWatch processes local device and process metadata, website requests, downloads, diagnostics and your privacy rights.
messages.privacy.lead: This policy distinguishes information processed on your device from requests handled by the website host, download providers and people you choose to contact.
messages.privacy.review: Review draft: the project operator and private contact address must be confirmed before publication. This page has not been approved for deployment.
messages.privacy.owner.title: 1. Project and responsibility
messages.privacy.owner.p1: MicCamWatch is free, open-source software maintained by Roman Cuisset and distributed through the project’s GitHub Releases. This policy covers the official application, this website and information voluntarily sent to the project. It describes the reviewed public version __MCW_VERSION__, not modified third-party builds.
messages.privacy.owner.p2: Roman Cuisset is the proposed contact and controller for processing whose purposes and means are determined by the project, such as website operation and correspondence; this role must be confirmed before this draft is published. Information that stays on your device is not received by the maintainer. If an organisation uses MCW, its own monitoring and data-protection responsibilities also apply.
messages.privacy.app.title: 2. What the application processes
messages.privacy.app.p1: MCW reads operating-system metadata about microphone and camera activity. Depending on the platform and permissions, this can include application names, process and parent IDs, executable paths, account or user IDs, session and integrity information, process ancestry, signing certificates or keys, capture-related module names, device names and identifiers, timestamps, and technical evidence or errors. Optional device-control journals can include USB topology, descriptors and hardware serial numbers. Some Windows checks inspect command lines in memory; raw command lines are not dedicated fields in the activity-event model.
messages.privacy.app.p2: The reviewed collectors do not record microphone audio, acquire webcam frames or inspect media payloads. Device discovery and activity/control metadata are not recordings. MCW uses the permissions exposed by the operating system; an unknown or degraded observation is not proof that access has stopped. Administrator approval and camera-profile inspection do not themselves grant camera or microphone capture permission.
messages.privacy.retention.title: 3. Storage and retention
messages.privacy.retention.p1: Local activity history is enabled by default. Where the selected frontend records events, it can store the metadata described above in history.jsonl. The current file rotates when it is already at least 5 MiB before the next event; three backups are retained and the oldest is replaced. This is size-based rotation, not an age-based deletion period or a strict total-size guarantee.
messages.privacy.retention.p2: Settings, policies, installation receipts and control/restoration journals are separate local files, generally retained until changed or explicitly removed. Successful restoration can clear owned entries; uncertain restoration can require keeping them. On macOS, helper observations and errors also pass through private temporary files, even with history disabled; normal cleanup removes them, but interrupted processes can leave files behind. Uninstallation is not a personal-data purge and normally preserves settings, policies and history.
messages.privacy.retention.p3: An explicitly selected watch log has no MCW-managed rotation or expiry. Optional operating-system event logs, desktop notifications, backups, synchronised folders and administrator-configured forwarding follow their own access and retention rules. Clearing MCW history does not clear these copies or restoration records. Do not delete restoration journals to bypass pending device restoration.
messages.privacy.retention.p4: No fixed retention period for this project’s Cloudflare hosting/security logs or GitHub download records could be established from the repository; the providers publish purpose- and legal-obligation-based criteria. Cloudflare separately documents seven days of unsampled Web Analytics data, followed by aggregation, with six months available in its interface; that is not a retention promise for all hosting logs. Public GitHub reports remain available until removed under the platform’s tools and policies; no fixed project retention schedule for private correspondence is established in this draft.
messages.privacy.network.title: 4. Application network activity
messages.privacy.network.p1: The reviewed monitoring code has no automatic uploader for activity history, observations, diagnostics or crash reports, and no startup or periodic update check was found. Explicit installation and update operations request scripts, release metadata, packages and checksums from this website or GitHub and its delivery infrastructure. On Windows, explicit portable uninstallation can also download the matching release to authenticate an installation with no ownership receipt. These services receive normal request metadata, including IP address, request time, client information and the requested resource; the inspected download calls do not attach monitoring history or policy files.
messages.privacy.network.p2: Signature verification defaults to the offline trust policy. If you select online trust, native certificate/revocation services or your GnuPG keyserver configuration can make requests while observations are assessed, disclosing the certificate or key being checked and connection metadata. Offline trust does not disable explicit downloads or control all operating-system, antivirus, proxy, DNS, backup or network-filesystem traffic. Package managers and source builds can also contact their own distribution services.
messages.privacy.website.title: 5. Website, cookies and Cloudflare
messages.privacy.website.p1: The site is hosted on Cloudflare Pages. Delivering and securing requests involves network metadata such as IP address, requested URL, time, browser/client information and technical or security results. The site’s own script enhances copying and navigation; it contains no cookie, localStorage or sessionStorage persistence, account system or report-submission form. No cookies or web-storage entries were observed in the browser check on __MCW_PRIVACY_UPDATED__. The delivered Permissions Policy disables website access to the microphone, camera and several other device features.
messages.privacy.website.p2: The public HTML includes a Cloudflare-injected Web Analytics beacon. In the check on __MCW_PRIVACY_UPDATED__, the delivered Content Security Policy blocked that external script; no successful analytics-beacon transmission was observed. This does not prevent Cloudflare from processing hosting requests. Cloudflare describes Web Analytics as a performance/page-view service without analytics cookies or individual cross-site tracking. Its hosting configuration must be reviewed before enabling or permitting any additional measurement; this policy and any legally required choices must then be updated.
messages.privacy.website.p3: The public responses also advertise Cloudflare Network Error Logging (NEL). Compatible browsers can send network-failure reports to Cloudflare, including request URL, error type, status, timing and network conditions. Cloudflare states that NEL uses the client IP transiently for network/geographic lookup and drops it after processing; this statement applies to the NEL pipeline, not every Cloudflare log. The browser policy lifetime in these headers is not a server-side data-retention period. No claim is made that hosting-provider processing is absent merely because application telemetry is absent.
messages.privacy.providers.title: 6. Recipients and international processing
messages.privacy.providers.p1: Cloudflare handles website hosting, delivery, security and its associated operational reporting. Its policy distinguishes processing on customers’ behalf from its own network/service purposes. GitHub hosts the repository, release downloads and voluntary issues or contributions. GitHub processes connection and usage information and, when you use an account or send content, the associated account and content data under its own policy. Ordinary page links are not embedded GitHub trackers; following a link or downloading a release starts a separate request.
messages.privacy.providers.p2: Cloudflare and GitHub operate internationally, including in the United States. Their policies describe the transfer mechanisms and safeguards they rely on, including relevant contractual clauses and Data Privacy Framework commitments. This page does not promise EU-only processing or invent a project-specific agreement. The operator must confirm the applicable hosting arrangements before publication. Information you publish in an issue can be read, copied or retained by other people.
messages.privacy.legal.title: 7. Purposes and legal bases
messages.privacy.legal.p1: For processing under the project operator’s responsibility, the proposed purposes and GDPR bases are: providing and protecting the public website, preventing abuse and handling voluntary project correspondence on the basis of legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(f)); and responding to applicable legal obligations and data-protection requests (Article 6(1)(c)). The interests are maintaining a usable, secure open-source project and addressing the requests people choose to send. The operator must confirm these purposes and bases before publication; third parties explain their own purposes and bases in their policies.
messages.privacy.legal.p2: Local monitoring serves the user’s chosen visibility and device-control purposes; it is not a feed of personal activity to the maintainer. Optional reporting and sharing are not required to download or use MCW. Normal connection information is necessary to deliver an online page or download. An operating-system permission or application setting must not be confused with GDPR consent. If a future processing activity relies on consent, it must provide the required information, a genuine choice and a way to withdraw it.
messages.privacy.rights.title: 8. Choices and your rights
messages.privacy.rights.p1: Use mcw config settings-path and mcw history path to locate the relevant local files. Set history_enabled to false and restart already-running monitoring frontends as needed to stop future history recording. mcw history clear removes the current MCW history and its rotated backups; it does not disable future recording, securely erase storage, or delete selected logs, operating-system records or control journals. You can stop monitoring and avoid online trust or optional logging; this does not erase existing copies.
messages.privacy.rights.p2: Where the GDPR applies and its conditions are met, you can request access, correction, erasure, restriction, objection and portability, and withdraw consent for processing based on consent. Send project-related requests through the private contact below, identifying the processing concerned without unnecessarily sharing sensitive logs. A request concerning data held only on your device cannot be fulfilled by accessing that device remotely. Cloudflare and GitHub also provide channels for processing under their own responsibility. You may complain to your competent supervisory authority; these rights are subject to applicable legal conditions and exceptions.
messages.privacy.reports.title: 9. Diagnostics, security and voluntary reports
messages.privacy.reports.p1: Diagnostics are displayed locally, not automatically submitted to the project. If you choose to send a log, screenshot, issue, email or antivirus submission, the recipient receives the content you provide. Review and redact names, account information, paths, device identifiers and other personal material first. Public issues are not a confidential channel. MCW does not provide automatic redaction, and operating-system crash reporting, cloud clipboard or backup features have separate policies. No sale, advertising upload or remote monitoring account feature was identified in the reviewed application and static site code.
messages.privacy.contact.title: 10. Privacy contact
messages.privacy.contact.p1: Use the private privacy contact published here for personal-data requests. Do not post private documents, full histories or identity evidence in a public GitHub issue. No privacy email address was verified in the inspected project; the maintainer must supply or confirm one before this draft is published.
messages.privacy.contact.pending: Private privacy contact address: awaiting confirmation before publication.
messages.privacy.changes.title: 11. Changes and sources
messages.privacy.changes.p1: This notice is based on the reviewed release source, the public website response and the providers’ documents available on the date above. Provider settings and future application versions can change the processing described here; material changes require a corresponding notice update. Unknown provider retention periods are not replaced with invented deadlines. Source links below let you inspect the underlying application and provider information.
messages.home.title.miccamwatch-surveillez-votre-: MicCamWatch — Monitor your microphone and camera
messages.home.p.eyebrow: A clearer view of your privacy.
messages.home.p.hero-lead: Spot access, understand the evidence, and take action from your desktop. MicCamWatch observes system metadata — not your conversations or images.
messages.home.p.hero-platforms:
Windows 10/11 · Linux x64 · macOS 15+
Native tool · Open source · No telemetry
messages.home.figcaption.le-vrai-menu-windows-cap: The actual Windows menu, captured in v0.17.1. Historical screenshot of the user installation: camera pipeline “ready”, microphone protection not requested, and camera allowed. A real interface, not evidence of capture or hardware blocking. It predates the incomplete-state diagnostics described in the Windows FAQ.
messages.home.h2.features-title:
A useful signal.
Not a magic promise.
messages.home.p.mcw-distingue-lactivite-observee-: MCW distinguishes observed activity, confidence level, and risk. Weak evidence does not become certainty.
messages.home.p.etat-instantane-suivi-en-direct-e: Current status, live monitoring, and a terminal dashboard. Process identity and context when the system makes them available.
messages.home.p.processus-chemin-origine-et-valid: Process, path, origin, and trust validation, depending on the OS. Diagnostics also show degraded or unavailable collectors.
messages.home.p.mute-commandes-camera-et-demarrag: Muting, camera commands, and launch at login: explicit actions limited to what the platform actually supports.
messages.home.aside.callout:
Remember

“ready” does not mean “active”. A loaded module, an available device, or an open handle does not prove a capture stream exists. A lack of observations does not prove a lack of access either.
messages.home.figcaption.sortie-reelle-de-mcw-top: Actual output from mcw top v0.17.1, run in Windows ConPTY in CI (150 columns), then rendered as an image. This runner has no capture devices, and its SDK mute state is unknown: it illustrates the interface, not detection or evidence of blocking on physical hardware. All screenshots on this page are from Windows.
messages.home.h2.scope-title:
The limits are part
of the product.
messages.home.p.la-surveillance-fonctionne-sans-d: Monitoring works without administrator privileges. Privileged actions require separate authorization.
messages.home.td.sessions-wasapi-actives-processu: Active WASAPI sessions; process validated when accessible.
messages.home.td.indices-natifs-de-capture-attrib: Native capture evidence; process attribution when available. Loaded modules: “ready” only.
messages.home.td.mute-des-endpoints-et-controle-d: Endpoint muting and camera device control with UAC. Manual protection is held in the background until explicitly released; no electrical isolation or guarantee for exclusive/ASIO paths.
messages.home.td.source-et-flux-en-cours-avec-lie: Source and running stream with an active link; PID authenticated, then validated in /proc.
messages.home.td.meme-exigence-de-lien-actif-pipe: The same active PipeWire link requirement applies. A V4L2 handle alone does not prove a stream exists; access outside PipeWire may go unobserved.
messages.home.td.mute-des-sources-de-la-session-p: Session source muting, not an ALSA access ban. USB uvcvideo cameras are supported only through a separate, reviewed administrator component; non-USB cameras are not supported.
messages.home.td.activite-dentree-coreaudio-pid-v: CoreAudio input activity; PID validated if the process identity is readable.
messages.home.td.etat-dexecution-du-peripherique-: Device running state via CoreMediaIO, medium confidence. Client and PID unknown. This signal does not prove an image stream exists; camera health is “degraded”.
messages.home.td.mute-uniquement-si-la-propriete-: Muting only if the input property is writable. MCW-owned camera profile, requiring manual approval in System Settings; its presence does not certify physical denial of access.
messages.home.p.pas-de-coupe-circuit-universel-mc: Not a universal kill switch. MCW is neither antivirus software nor forensic proof of capture. A protected process, driver, direct access, or inaccessible session can limit observations and controls. WSL, virtual machines, and runners without hardware do not guarantee access to physical devices.
messages.home.p.ressources-objectif-15-mo-non-att: Resources: the 15 MB target has not been met. Documented measurements for the full Windows scenario exceed this target (sampled combined peak RSS: 56,041 MB, using a decimal comma). These measurements have limitations; no memory budget guarantee is claimed. Read the measurements and their scope ↗
messages.home.p.version-stable-mcw-version-les-ex: Version __MCW_VERSION__. Links target this release on GitHub, never a mirror on this site. Install only after its packages, checksums and provenance have been published; a source tag alone does not establish availability.
messages.home.h3.une-ligne-pour-suivre-la-version: The Unix installer, in one line.
messages.home.p.code-note: This command executes a remote script. Downloading and reading it first is safer. This is not a PowerShell command: on Windows, choose the MSI or ZIP below.
messages.home.p.installer-origin-note: Without JavaScript or in an HTTP preview, the HTTPS link points to the script at the release’s immutable commit. On this site over HTTPS, the command is adapted to its local install.sh endpoint. Archives and their checksums are still downloaded from GitHub.
messages.home.p.small-text: Commands remain selectable without JavaScript. The “Copy” button appears only if the browser provides its secure clipboard API; otherwise, select the text and use Ctrl+C, Cmd+C, or the selection menu.
messages.home.p.le-msi-par-utilisateur-ajoute-mcw: The per-user MSI adds mcw to PATH and a shortcut to the Start menu. The portable ZIP contains the CLI + tray host pair; keep these two executables together and at the same version. In 0.20, the Windows executables, MSI shortcut and Apps entry use the official application icon.
messages.home.p.small-text-2: Reopen PowerShell after installation. For a ZIP installation not added to PATH, use .\mcw.exe instead of mcw.
messages.home.aside.inline-warning: Unsigned public release. The __MCW_VERSION__ EXEs and MSI have no Authenticode signature. SHA-256 checksums and attestations are neither a signed publisher identity nor an antivirus verdict. Do not disable Defender to install MCW. See the precautions.
messages.home.p.requiert-les-bibliotheques-pipewi: Requires PipeWire/SPA libraries, pw-dump, and an accessible PipeWire socket in your user session. The tray requires a StatusNotifierItem host; notifications and sound require their session services.
messages.home.p.linstallateur-gere-lexecutable-so: The installer manages the executable under $HOME/.local/bin by default and checks the archive’s exact entry in SHA256SUMS. Unsupported architectures are rejected, not substituted.
messages.home.aside.inline-warning-2: This command does not install USB camera controls. They require a separate, reviewed administrator installation of the same version, followed by explicit Polkit authorization. PipeWire muting does not block direct ALSA paths. Read the procedure and its limits ↗.
messages.home.p.linstallateur-selectionne-votre-a: The installer selects your native architecture. The menu bar requires an Aqua session. The native helper is bundled; no development environment is required for these archives.
messages.home.p.macos-app-install: Download the DMG for your processor, mount it, and drag MicCamWatch.app into /Applications. Open the copied app to start directly in the menu bar, without Terminal. No autostart, protection or permission is enabled implicitly.
messages.home.p.macos-app-replace: To update, quit MCW and replace the whole app at the same location; preferences and history remain outside it. Refresh only an explicitly owned login registration with autostart refresh from the bundled CLI. mcw update refuses partial app replacement.
messages.home.aside.inline-warning-3: No Apple Developer ID signature or notarization. The helper’s ad hoc signature does not certify the publisher. MCW does not bypass Gatekeeper, SIP, TCC, or quarantine. If the system blocks launch, do not remove these protections: consult the provenance and signing information. The camera still has no PID attribution.
messages.home.p.linux-et-macos-ce-script-est-epin: Linux and macOS · This script is pinned to the release commit. Download and read it first; verify its checksum before running the separate installation command below.
messages.home.p.avant-execution-comparez-la-somme: Before execution, compare the file’s checksum: sha256sum mcw-install.sh on Linux, or shasum -a 256 mcw-install.sh on macOS. The expected value for the installer script (not the archives) is:
messages.home.p.small-text-3: A checksum displayed through the same channel verifies byte consistency, not independent authenticity. Also consult the script at its immutable source.
messages.home.p.apres-lecture-et-verification-ins: After reading and verification, install version __MCW_VERSION__, explicitly requesting that it be added to PATH:
messages.home.p.small-text-4: Replace --add-path with --no-modify-path to leave the shell configuration unchanged. Without a choice, the installer asks for consent in a terminal; it does not silently change PATH in non-interactive mode. Then open a new terminal. No automatic startup or device control is enabled.
messages.home.p.small-text-5: Expected result on Unix: the script displays the download and verification steps, then Installation completed: mcw __MCW_VERSION__ for the explicitly requested version. Steps are colored in a compatible terminal (disable with NO_COLOR). It then explains how to run mcw top and, if necessary, use the full path or open a new terminal for PATH. This success concerns installation: it certifies neither device availability nor active protection.
messages.home.p.telechargez-votre-archive-et-sha2: Download your archive and SHA256SUMS from the same release. On Linux, use sha256sum --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS. On macOS, compare the output of shasum -a 256 miccamwatch-macos-aarch64.tar.gz (Apple Silicon) or shasum -a 256 miccamwatch-macos-x86_64.tar.gz (Intel) with the exact manifest entry. In PowerShell, Get-FileHash .\miccamwatch-windows-x86_64.zip -Algorithm SHA256 lets you compare the ZIP checksum (adjust the name for the MSI).
messages.home.p.les-attestations-github-renseigne: GitHub attestations provide build provenance information. To verify with GitHub CLI, adjust the path to the downloaded file:
messages.home.p.sommes-et-archives-partagent-le-c: Checksums and archives share the publication channel. Build provenance, publisher signing, and antivirus analysis are three different things. This site serves no binaries.
messages.home.p.availability-note: Homebrew / AUR: recipes exist in the repository; no published tap or AUR package is announced. Do not use an invented package-manager command.
messages.home.p.linstallation-seule-nactive-aucun: Installation alone enables no protection, autostart, or process termination.
messages.home.p.affichez-la-version-letat-des-col: Display the version, collector status, and observed access. status returns 0 with no matching access, 1 with access, and 2 on error: exit code 1 is not a failure.
messages.home.p.top-ouvre-le-tableau-de-bord-tray: top opens the dashboard. tray opens the native menu (Windows notification area, Linux StatusNotifierItem, macOS menu bar). In 0.20, macOS also has a single native consultation window for observed state, access details and diagnostics, plus a localized About window. Closing the consultation window leaves the tray running; reopening the app reuses the window. The simplified menu retains protection, pause and all four profiles, with a larger, proportionate mark and distinct state badges. Stop terminal monitoring with Ctrl+C.
messages.home.p.seulement-si-vous-le-souhaitez-en: Only if you want to, register the tray to launch at login: Windows user task/entry, Linux .desktop file, or macOS LaunchAgent. No login service is installed implicitly.
messages.home.aside.callout-2:
Controls are explicit

mcw mute and mcw camera block request actions with the scope described above. Then check mcw mute --status and mcw camera status. A request, a software state, and an observation are three distinct facts. A pending operation or pending macOS profile approval does not mean “protected”.
messages.home.p.guide-footnote: Automatic termination (--kill-unauthorized) is disabled by default. It requires explicit denial by a publisher/path policy, attributed active capture, two consecutive observations, and an unprotected process. A “suspicious” risk alone does not enable it; a macOS camera without a PID cannot trigger it.
messages.home.p.eyebrow-7: An installation you remain in control of
messages.home.p.ne-melangez-pas-msi-installateur-: Do not mix MSI, managed installer, manual archive, and package manager installations. The installation owner determines the procedure.
messages.home.aside.inline-warning-important-warn: Before replacing or removing executables: explicitly release the protections you requested (mcw unmute, mcw camera allow), check their status and wait for full restoration, then stop the watcher and tray (mcw tray stop). Closing the tray or terminal does not release Windows protection held in the background. A pending restoration must be resolved, not ignored. The portable updater’s safety measures do not cover external MSI/manual replacement.
messages.home.li.windows-msi-installez-le-msi-de-: Windows MSI: install the MSI from the new release; mcw update does not update the MSI registration.
messages.home.li.windows-portable-cargo-mcw-updat: Windows portable / Cargo: mcw update verifies and replaces a consistent CLI/tray pair after validating protection readiness and safely stopping the owned tray.
messages.home.li.unix-gere-mcw-update-ou-le-scrip: Managed Unix: mcw update or the public script with the same prefix. Without --version, the script follows stable latest. The updater rejects downgrades.
messages.home.li.archive-manuelle-linux-necessite: Manual archive: Linux requires manual replacement; macOS can update an owned standalone executable outside bin under the documented conditions.
messages.home.li.gestionnaire-de-paquets-mettez-a: Package manager: update with that manager, never with the curl script or mcw update. For an existing owned Homebrew login registration, run HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_CLEANUP=1 brew upgrade miccamwatch && mcw autostart refresh && brew cleanup miccamwatch as the ordinary user. Stop on failure; never clean up the old keg before refresh succeeds. Refresh preserves loaded, dormant and disabled intent, refuses unrelated entries and never enables absent intent. Without an existing registration, ordinary Homebrew upgrade needs no refresh.
messages.home.p.small-text-6: Managed updates preserve preferences and do not re-enable absent, disabled, or external autostart entries. An installation that is modified, active, or whose ownership cannot be verified is rejected; do not force a workaround.
messages.home.li.windows-msi-desactivez-lautostar: Windows MSI / Cargo: mcw uninstall returns exit code 2 and reports the exact manager procedure without claiming removal: msiexec.exe /x {product-code} or cargo uninstall --root "INSTALL-ROOT" miccamwatch. These placeholders are not runnable commands: use the exact values reported for this installation. Resolve protection, disable owned autostart and exit normally before using the manager.
messages.home.li.zip-portable-desactivez-lautosta: Windows portable ZIP: mcw uninstall verifies this exact CLI/tray pair using its ownership receipt (older ZIPs require the same-version verified public package). An authenticated worker waits for normal CLI exit and records actual removal in its local result.json; accepted deferred work is not completed deletion.
messages.home.li.unix-gere-apres-telechargement-e: Managed Unix: mcw uninstall reuses this installation's receipt and unchanged PATH blocks; no prefix guessing. The reviewed script remains available as sh mcw-install.sh --uninstall --prefix 'EXACT-PREFIX' after normal process exit; substitute the recorded prefix. Homebrew/AUR stay manager-owned: the command returns exit code 2 with the exact manager instructions, not removal success. After restoring protection, disabling owned autostart and quitting, use brew uninstall --formula miccamwatch / sudo pacman -R -- miccamwatch only for an installation actually owned by that manager, with the exact package reported. This does not announce a published tap or AUR package.
messages.home.li.composant-camera-linux-restaurez: Linux camera component: restore owned bindings and explicitly remove the separate administrator component before updating or removing the user installation. Procedure ↗.
messages.home.p.small-text-7: MCW ≥ 0.20: requested/active protection, pending or unknown restoration, an elevated operation, a privileged helper, changed/foreign/linked payloads cause refusal before shutdown. Explicitly restore first; uninstall never unmutes or allows cameras. Only unchanged owned autostart/payload/receipt/PATH entries are removed; settings, history and policy remain. A macOS .app is not deleted automatically: use this exact app's CLI to restore and disable owned autostart, quit it, then move the whole app identified by the command to Trash (or use its MDM owner). Standalone macOS copies receive an exact-file manual procedure, not automatic success.
messages.home.p.privacy-lead: No audio recording or image capture. No telemetry or history sent to a server.
messages.home.p.mcw-lit-les-signaux-du-systeme-et: MCW reads system signals and process information. Settings, policies, logs, and history stay local. Check the paths with mcw config settings-path and mcw history path; mcw history clear clears MCW history.
messages.home.p.installation-et-mise-a-jour-conta: Installation and updates contact GitHub. An “online” trust policy allows native network checks of certificates or keys; “offline” prohibits them according to the platform. System logs follow their own retention rules.
messages.home.p.pas-de-tracker-pas-de-bibliothequ: The site uses local assets and optional JavaScript, without remote fonts. Cloudflare injects a Web Analytics script, blocked by the current Content Security Policy in the reviewed version, and supplies network-error reporting through response headers. Hosting and GitHub process request metadata; see the privacy policy for the distinctions.
messages.home.p.commencez-par-mcw-doctor-un-colle: Start with mcw doctor. An unavailable collector is not an all-clear.
messages.home.p.ouvrez-un-nouveau-terminal-apres-: Open a new terminal after a PATH change. On portable Windows, use .\mcw.exe from the extracted folder. On Unix, try "$HOME/.local/bin/mcw" --version if you kept the default prefix. The installer cannot change its parent terminal’s environment.
messages.home.p.si-defender-a-mis-lexecutable-en-: If Defender quarantined the executable, PATH is not the problem: keep the Protection history details and follow the precautions below without restoring the detected bytes.
messages.home.summary.windows-camera-utilisee-pid: Windows: camera in use, unknown PID, or partial coverage in the tray
messages.home.p.une-activite-camera-peut-rester-s: Camera activity may remain without an attributed PID when the native report provides no usable timestamp, even if Windows supplies a raw PID. Since version 0.17.2, the tray retains observed access and marks this partial coverage with an orange exclamation mark. Details identify the collector, its reason, and captures; genuine unavailability or a protection error still takes priority. Older versions may display a gray cross and a generic “telemetry degraded” summary.
messages.home.p.consultez-status-details-mcw-stat: Check Status details…, mcw status --lang fr, mcw status --json, and mcw doctor to distinguish activity, attribution, and collector health. Unknown attribution means neither “no access” nor “camera blocked”: no client identity or authority to stop a process should be inferred from its name alone or a raw PID. The screenshots on this page remain explicitly historical, from 0.17.1.
messages.home.summary.quels-droits-et-permissions: What privileges and permissions are needed?
messages.home.p.observer-lancez-mcw-dans-votre-se: Observation: run MCW in your user session without general elevation. System restrictions can make some identities or collectors unavailable; additional privileges do not guarantee attribution.
messages.home.p.windows-les-changements-de-periph: Windows: camera device changes require separate UAC authorization. Linux: USB camera controls first require the separate administrator component of the same version, then explicit Polkit authorization; the user installer does not deploy it. macOS: installing and removing the camera profile remain manual operations in System Settings, and notifications depend on system permission. MCW does not bypass TCC, Gatekeeper, or SIP; a profile’s presence does not prove capture is denied.
messages.home.summary.linux-pipewire-indisponible: Linux: PipeWire unavailable, no camera, or no tray
messages.home.p.lancez-mcw-dans-votre-session-uti: Run MCW in your desktop user session, not through sudo. Check pw-dump, PipeWire/SPA libraries, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, the user socket, and PIPEWIRE_REMOTE if customized. An inaccessible or restarting socket is an error, not “no access”.
messages.home.p.le-tray-requiert-un-hote-statusno: The tray requires a StatusNotifierItem host. Notifications need the session service and notify-send; sound needs canberra-gtk-play, a theme, and a session backend. An accepted call does not certify that a notification was seen or a sound heard. Direct camera access outside PipeWire may remain unattributed or degrade observation.
messages.home.summary.macos-pourquoi-la-camera-na: macOS: why does the camera have no PID?
messages.home.p.lapi-publique-coremediaio-indique: The public CoreMediaIO API reports the device’s running state, not the identity of the client using it. MCW therefore displays an unknown PID and degraded camera health rather than inventing attribution. AVFoundation availability and running state do not prove images were captured. Pending profile approval does not count as blocking.
messages.home.summary.smartscreen-defender-ou-gat: SmartScreen, Defender, or Gatekeeper: should I bypass them?
messages.home.p.non-ne-desactivez-pas-les-protect: No: do not disable protections or add an exclusion. The public __MCW_VERSION__ release is unsigned on Windows; no Apple Developer ID signature or notarization is announced. Warnings may therefore appear. A GitHub attestation describes a build, not its safety.
messages.home.p.en-cas-de-detection-defender-note: If Defender detects something, record the name, path, version, available hash, and Protection history details. Do not restore the quarantined file or automatically reinstall the detected bytes. The repository documents the incident and manual submission to Microsoft; no false-positive verdict is claimed. Signing, provenance, and safe handling ↗.
messages.home.summary.jai-ferme-le-tray-mes-prote: I closed the tray: have my protections been removed?
messages.home.p.pas-necessairement-sous-windows-u: Not necessarily. On Windows, manual protection belongs to a native background broker and remains requested after closing the tray or top, until mcw unmute or mcw camera allow. This does not promise persistence across a restart. Linux and macOS retain their limited, one-shot controls: they do not inherit this Windows mechanism.
messages.home.p.verifiez-le-statut-reel-une-garde: Check the actual status. A stopped Windows camera guard remains a warning: a “Block” intent alone does not prove protection of future connections. Explicitly restore before replacement or uninstallation, and resolve any pending state.
messages.home.summary.pourquoi-une-mise-a-jour-ou: Why is an update or uninstall rejected?
messages.home.p.un-executable-actif-une-protectio: An active executable, requested protection, pending restoration, missing/modified receipt, or unsafe path can prevent an operation. Stop your watchers, complete privileged operations, and check control status. The script rejects root, modified/unowned targets, and unsafe links; it does not stop processes for you.
messages.home.p.un-ancien-tray-peut-necessiter-un: An older tray may require a normal manual exit: do not force it to quit during a camera operation. Do not delete ownership records to bypass rejection. Use the appropriate installation owner and the documented procedure.
messages.home.summary.comment-partager-un-diagnos: How can I share diagnostics without exposing my private information?
messages.home.p.mcw-doctor-json-et-mcw-status-jso: mcw doctor --json and mcw status --json help with diagnostics, but paths, users, PIDs, devices, and application names may be personal information. Review and redact this data before attaching an excerpt to an issue. MCW does not automatically collect your reports; sharing remains voluntary. Technical evidence details stay in English to keep diagnostics stable.
